definitions.explanation: The Japanese five-yen coin. Distinctive for its brass color and the hole in the center. Often used as an offering at Shinto shrines because ごえん sounds like ご{縁|えん} (good ties, favorable connections).

examples.japanese: ⟦{財布|さいふ}→財布：00663_saifu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{五円玉|ごえんだま}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一枚|いちまい}→一枚：08889_ichimai⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There was one 5-yen coin in my wallet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{五円玉|ごえんだま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{賽銭箱|さいせんばこ}→賽銭箱：24468_saisenbako⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れて→入れる：01098_ireru⟧⟦お{参|まい}り→お参り：16837_omairi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I put a 5-yen coin in the offertory box at the shrine and prayed.

examples.japanese: {五円玉|ごえんだま}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「⟦ご{縁|えん}→ご縁：08773_goen⟧」⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|つう}じる→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧、⟦{縁起|えんぎ}→縁起：13815_engi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{初詣|はつもうで}→初詣：05804_hatsumoude⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧お⟦{賽銭|さいせん}→賽銭：05958_saisen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{好|この}まれる→好む：02103_konomu⟧。
examples.english: The 5-yen coin is considered auspicious because it sounds like 'good ties' (ご縁), and is often preferred for New Year shrine offerings.

notes:
The five-yen coin (brass, with a hole) is the only Japanese coin with a hole in the center. Its pronunciation ごえん is a homophone of ⟦ご{縁|えん}→ご縁：08773_goen⟧ (good fortune, beneficial connections), making it a popular coin for shrine offerings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {五円玉|ごえんだま}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{投|な}げる→投げる：01135_nageru⟧: to toss a 5-yen coin (into the offertory box)
- {五円玉|ごえんだま}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦お{参|まい}り→お参り：16837_omairi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to pray using a 5-yen coin
- {穴|あな}あき⟦{硬貨|こうか}→硬貨：02745_kouka⟧: perforated coin (a description of the 5-yen coin)

CULTURAL NOTE: The punning connection between ごえん (five yen) and ⟦ご{縁|えん}→ご縁：08773_goen⟧ (good fortune, fate, relationships) makes this coin uniquely popular for shrine offerings, especially at ⟦{初詣|はつもうで}→初詣：05804_hatsumoude⟧ (New Year shrine visits).
